title: python -m ai_router.progress --json (the Work Explorer's projection)
description: Everything the extension renders for one repository, in one pass, as ai_router.progress.build_projection returns it. It is a read, not a record: nothing on disk is written in this shape, and it is recomputed on every call. The schema exists because the extension's view of it was a hand-kept TypeScript mirror, which is the drift this file removes -- from here the mirror is generated from this. Nothing here is derived on the reading side: the padding of a number, the words of a state, and the headline of a terminal round are all decided in Python, and a reader that recomputed one of them would be a second implementation of a rule.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this payload is written in.

generatedAt.description: When the projection was computed, local time with offset.

sessionStatus.description: The one status vocabulary, shared by sessions and tasks.

orchestrator.description: Who ran the sessions, passed through from the ledger's orchestrator block rather than re-shaped. Open, because the block carries more than a reader needs and a closed copy here would be a second declaration of it.

repository.description: The repository-level half. There is no status: nothing above a session carries a lifecycle state, so a repository has a progress fraction and nothing else.

sessionsSource.description: Where these sessions came from. 'ledger' is the machine-written record; 'plan' is a repository that has been set up and never run, whose sessions are the ones its plan declares.

invariantViolation.description: Two sessions in flight, or another state the ledger may not be in. Rendered, never repaired.

task.description: One step of an in-flight session's approved plan, folded with its execution record. Identity and order are the plan's; state and iconKey come from step-execution.jsonl.

isOpen.description: The one step in flight, if this is it. At most one per session.

fidelity.description: 'verbatim' / 'transformed' / 'unverified', or null when the row was written before fidelity was recorded.

agency.description: What the verifier looked at in the round that stopped a session, and how faithfully. mode is null for a round recorded before the agency log existed -- unknown, which is not the same as 'none'.

finding.description: One finding as the record carries it, with the record's own word for how it stands.

disposition.description: 'outstanding' / 'fixed, unreviewed' / 'noted' -- the fold's words, not a reader's.

verification.description: A session's rounds ledger folded for reading at planning time: which terminal state was reached, how it reads, and whether the row is clean. Carried for every session that has rounds, not only the in-flight one.

terminal.description: VERIFIED, ISSUES_FOUND (unresolved at the cap) or REMEDIATED_AT_CAP; null while the loop is still open.

headline.description: The one sentence every loop reports its state in, written in Python.

displayNumber.description: The number as the projection wrote it -- '015'. Python owns the padding rule; this is its result, not a shape a reader re-derives. Empty when an older router sent no name.

tasksRefused.description: Why the execution record could not be read. A refusal is not an empty task list: the view must say it cannot tell which step is open rather than render the last row it could read.
